tools.description: Search the product knowledge vault by free-text query. Useful when you need product knowledge but don't yet know which concept ids exist. Returns ranked hits (id, title, type, score, snippet) only; get_concept returns one full note and get_context an assembled briefing. An empty hit list means nothing matched.

mode.description: Search mode. "hybrid" (default) fuses keyword and semantic ranking; semantic silently falls back to keyword if embeddings are unavailable.

product.description: Only return concepts belonging to this product.

query.description: Free-text search query, e.g. "lead scoring" or "session auth".

tags.description: Only return concepts carrying ALL of these tags.

type.description: Only return concepts of this type.

tools.name: search_concepts
tools.title: Search concepts

tools.description: Fetch one concept by exact id: full markdown body, metadata, and its direct graph neighbors (each with the relation that connects it). Use after search_concepts or when another note wiki-links an id you need in full. The neighbors list tells you what to fetch next. If you don't know the id, use search_concepts instead.
tools.name: get_concept
tools.title: Get concept

tools.description: Walk the knowledge graph outward from a concept and return everything within `depth` hops, with distance and the edge path that reached it. Use to map the blast radius before changing a feature (what depends on it, what constrains it, which decisions apply) or to discover structure that keyword search misses. Filter by relation names (e.g. depends_on) to follow only one kind of edge.

depth.description: How many hops to traverse (1-3, default 1).

relations.description: Only follow edges with these relation names, e.g. ["depends_on", "part_of"].

tools.name: get_related
tools.title: Get related concepts

tools.description: Assemble a markdown briefing of the concepts most relevant to a query and/or explicit ids, expanded through the graph and trimmed to a token budget. The briefing is self-contained, so it can be handed to another agent or pasted into a prompt as-is. The final JSON line reports which concept ids were included, whether the bundle was truncated, and its approximate token count. Provide at least one of `query` or `ids`.

depth.description: Graph hops to expand from the seeds (default 1).

ids.description: Explicit seed concept ids (kept first, in order).

product.description: Restrict expansion to concepts of this product.

query.description: Search query used to pick seed concepts.

tokenBudget.description: Approximate token cap for the bundle (chars/4, default 4000).

tools.name: get_context
tools.title: Assemble context bundle

tools.description: Write a concept note into the vault (creates or overwrites the markdown file, then reindexes it). Use to capture new product knowledge discovered during a task — a decision made, a constraint hit, a pattern adopted — so future agents can find it. Omit `id` to derive a slug from the title; pass an existing id to update that note. Body is markdown; [[wiki-links]] to other concept ids create graph edges. Returns the saved concept's metadata.

body.description: Markdown body. [[other-id]] wiki-links become graph edges.

codeAreas.description: Rough codebase paths/globs where this knowledge lives, e.g. ["packages/core/src/vault.ts", "apps/web/src/routes/**"] — lets agents briefed by get_context know where to apply it.

doneAt.description: For tasks: ISO timestamp when completed.

id.description: Concept id (slug). Omit to derive from title; pass an existing id to update.

relations.description: Typed edges, e.g. {"depends_on": ["auth-system"]}. Conventions: part_of (feature/story/task → domain), realized_by (story → features), realizes (task → stories/features), governs (spec → what it constrains), governed_by (task → specs), depends_on, constrains, supersedes, related_to. For domain concepts, prefer linking to OTHER domains (related_to / depends_on) wherever they share a boundary or hand off responsibility — connected domains reveal how the product's areas overlap instead of floating as isolated islands.

takenAt.description: For tasks: ISO timestamp when claimed.

takenBy.description: For tasks: label of the agent/orchestrator that claimed it.

taskStatus.description: For type="task" concepts: lifecycle "open" | "taken" | "done" (default "open"). Prefer the task tools (create_task / take_task / complete_task) over setting this directly.

type.description: Concept type (default "concept"). The 11 built-in types are concept, domain, feature, story, spec, workflow, task, decision, constraint, pattern, glossary; a vault may also define custom types. An unknown type falls back to "concept".

tools.name: upsert_concept
tools.title: Create or update concept

tools.description: Remove a concept from the vault and all of its outgoing edges. Use to clear a note that is wrong, obsolete, or junk (e.g. a probe or test node that shouldn't be in the graph). Idempotent: deleting an id that doesn't exist is a no-op success (deleted:false), not an error. Deletion is permanent — prefer upsert_concept to correct a note you want to keep. Returns { deleted, id }.

id.description: Exact concept id (slug) to delete, e.g. "lead-scoring".

tools.name: delete_concept
tools.title: Delete concept

tools.description: Add a typed, directed edge between two existing concepts by editing the `from` note's frontmatter (e.g. lead-scoring depends_on contact-model). Use when you notice a relationship the vault is missing. Both concepts should already exist; use upsert_concept first if not.

from.description: Source concept id (its file gains the relation).

relation.description: Edge type, e.g. part_of | realized_by | governs | depends_on | constrains | supersedes | related_to (default). Domain→domain links (related_to / depends_on) are encouraged where two domains share a boundary, so the graph shows how areas overlap.

tools.name: link_concepts
tools.title: Link concepts

tools.description: Enumerate concept metadata (no bodies), optionally filtered by product, type, or a single tag. Use to get the lay of the land in an unfamiliar vault, to audit what exists (e.g. all decisions for a product), or when search vocabulary isn't matching. For content, follow up with get_concept or get_context.
tools.name: list_concepts
tools.title: List concepts

tools.description: Summarize the vault: counts of concepts and edges, the products and tags in use, a breakdown by concept type, and whether semantic search is available. Useful for gauging how much knowledge is here and which product/tag filters exist.
tools.name: vault_stats
tools.title: Vault stats

tools.description: Index an existing product's codebase into this vault. {action: "start"} returns the onboarding playbook: a method for surveying the codebase and recording its product knowledge (domains, features, stories, specs, workflows, decisions, constraints) as concepts via upsert_concept, each anchored to the code with codeAreas. {action: "status", areaList} reports onboarded state, concept counts and, given your repo's source areas (Brainz can't read the repo), which areas are covered or uncovered. {action: "complete", summary, areaList} marks the vault onboarded and stores the summary; it is rejected while too many areas are uncovered. Until onboarding completes, search_concepts and get_context results include a one-line note saying so.

action.description: "start" returns the onboarding playbook, "complete" marks the vault onboarded (requires `summary`), "status" reports onboarded state and concept counts.

areaList.description: With "status" or "complete": the repo's top-level source areas (packages/*, apps/*/src subtrees, major dirs) from your own repo walk — Brainz can't read the repo. "status" diffs concepts' code_areas against this to report covered vs uncovered areas; "complete" is REJECTED if too many areas are still uncovered.

productName.description: With "start": the product's name, echoed into the playbook heading.

repoHint.description: With "start": where the codebase lives (path or URL), echoed into the playbook.

summary.description: Required with "complete": 2–5 sentences on what was indexed and any notable gaps — stored as the product-onboarding-summary concept.

tools.name: onboard
tools.title: Onboard this vault

annotations.title: Sync this vault to the current code

tools.description: Re-index an onboarded vault after the code changes (drift). {action: "start"} returns the sync playbook: the vault's last_synced_at, a coverage map over the concepts' code_areas, and a method for re-indexing only what changed (you run git — Brainz can't read the repo — and pass back changedPaths + areaList): update stale concepts in place, add concepts or tasks for new work, and report coverage gaps. {action: "status", areaList} reports onboarded state, last sync time, staleness, concept counts and coverage. {action: "complete", summary, areaList} stamps last_synced_at and appends the summary to the product-onboarding-summary concept (a running sync log). After ~14 days without a sync, get_context and search results include a one-line note saying so.

action.description: "start" returns the sync (re-onboard) playbook — a DRIFT playbook scoped to what changed since the last sync (NOT the full onboarding playbook). "complete" records last_synced_at and appends the summary to the running sync log (requires `summary`). "status" reports onboarded state, last sync time, concept counts, staleness, and (with areaList) coverage.

areaList.description: With "start", "status", or "complete": the repo's top-level source areas from your own repo walk (Brainz can't read the repo). Used to compute the coverage map (covered vs uncovered areas) — "complete" is REJECTED if too many areas are still uncovered.

changedPaths.description: With "start": paths you found CHANGED since last_synced_at (from your own git diff/log). The playbook focuses the fan-out on the areas these fall under.

productName.description: With "start": the product's name, echoed into the playbook heading.

summary.description: Required with "complete": 2–5 sentences on what changed, what you updated, and what you indexed — APPENDED to the product-onboarding-summary concept as a running sync log (never overwritten).

tools.name: sync
tools.title: Sync this vault to the current code

tools.description: Dreaming: a scheduled consolidation sweep over this vault. Light stages what changed since the last dream (near-duplicate concepts, finished task outcomes, hygiene counts); REM asks an LLM for proposals; deep applies the ones that pass threshold gates: merges duplicates (edges redirected, the other tombstoned), promotes outcome knowledge into concepts, adds missing links, and files a task for each contradiction. A sweep that would touch too much of the vault is rejected; every applied dream keeps preimages and can be reverted. {action: "status"} shows schedule + last dream; {action: "run"} dreams now; {action: "diary"} reads the Dream Diary; {action: "revert", id} undoes one dream; {action: "configure", enabled?, cadenceHours?} sets it up. Without an LLM only light runs.

action.description: "status" reports whether dreaming is on, its cadence, the last/next dream and any sweep in flight. "run" starts (or continues) a sweep NOW and advances it as far as one request allows. "diary" returns recent Dream Diary entries (newest first). "revert" undoes one dream via its preimages (requires `id`). "configure" turns dreaming on/off and sets the cadence.

enabled.description: With "configure": turn nightly dreaming on or off.

id.description: With "revert": the dream id to undo (from "diary" or "status").

limit.description: With "diary": how many entries to return (default 10).

tools.name: dream
tools.title: Dream (nightly consolidation)

tools.description: List the vault's work pile: `task`-type concepts with their lifecycle (open/taken/done), oldest first, including who has taken each one (takenBy). Filter by taskStatus or by the domain the tasks are part_of. Read-only; take_task is what claims a task.

domain.description: Only tasks that are part_of this domain concept id.

taskStatus.description: Only tasks in this lifecycle state ("open" | "taken" | "done"). Omit for all.

tools.name: list_tasks
tools.title: List tasks

annotations.title: Take a task off the pile

tools.description: Claim a task and get its briefing in one call. Pass an `id` to claim a specific task, or omit it to claim the next open task (oldest open by createdAt then id). Atomically flips the task to "taken" and records takenBy/takenAt; errors if it's already taken or done. Returns the task and a get_context-style briefing for its part_of domain plus the concepts it realizes / is governed_by (with code_areas). complete_task marks it done.

id.description: Claim this specific task by id. Omit to claim THE next open task (oldest by createdAt then id).

takenBy.description: Label for who's claiming it (agent/orchestrator name). Defaults to a generic label.

tools.name: take_task
tools.title: Take a task off the pile

tools.description: Mark a task done. Sets taskStatus=done + doneAt and appends `outcome` to the task body as an Outcome section. The result carries a one-line `reminder` that the rest of the graph is not updated automatically.

id.description: Id of the task to mark done.

outcome.description: A short account of what was done — appended to the task body as an Outcome section.

tools.name: complete_task
tools.title: Complete a task

tools.description: Turn a finding into first-class work: creates a `task`-type concept with taskStatus=open and the given relations — part_of a domain, `realizes` stories/features, `governed_by` specs — plus codeAreas pointing at where the work lands. Use when you discover work that isn't reflected in the codebase yet (a gap, a needed fix, a follow-up). The task then shows up in list_tasks / take_task and on the Kanban board.

body.description: Markdown description of the work. [[wiki-links]] become edges.

codeAreas.description: Rough codebase paths/globs where the work lands.

domain.description: Domain concept id this task is part_of.

governedBy.description: Spec concept ids that govern this task (creates `governed_by` edges).

realizes.description: Story/feature concept ids this task realizes (creates `realizes` edges).

tags.description: Tags, e.g. a priority tag like "high" or an area tag.

tools.name: create_task
tools.title: Create a task
